new.headline: Heat, 5.5 hours of sleep and a work crunch stacked up on you, so next week is a reset: no made-up miles, one lighter quality session, and a long run only if the body cooperates.

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer: No, do not make up the miles. Chasing lost volume on top of poor sleep, heat and a work deadline is how small issues turn into injuries or a stalled block. The plan is already written: this is 8 weeks out, so one honest reset week costs you nothing and protects the long runs that actually matter in the next month.

new.analysis:
## Why this week looks the way it does

The numbers tell the story: same routes, same effort, but your easy heart rate climbed 13 beats and your threshold pace felt like a 9/10. That is not fitness lost, that is heat plus 5.5 hours of sleep plus a work deadline all landing in one week. The right response is to lower the stress you can control.

So I have kept the shape of your week but softened it. Quality is replaced with easy running plus strides, which keeps leg speed without digging a hole. The long run comes back toward where it was two weeks ago, not where you were "supposed" to be, with a firm cap on heart rate rather than distance.

Two things to watch during the week. First, if the AC is fixed and sleep gets back to 7 hours, you should feel the Tuesday run come back toward 138 to 142 bpm at your usual easy pace; that is my green light that the next week can push again. Second, treat heart rate, not pace, as the governor on the long run: if you cross 150 before mile 8, slow down or walk a minute, even if the pace looks slow on screen.

One note on the knee from two weeks ago: no pain reported since, which is good. Keep the hip and glute work going, even just 10 minutes twice this week, because that was the pattern that kept it quiet before.

settingsProposalBullets: Note that the apartment AC was out through late August 2026, which likely drove the heat-related jump in easy heart rate.
Add a standing 10 to 15 minute hip and glute routine twice a week, since it coincided with the knee staying quiet.

safetyCallouts.title: Sleep and heat strain.
safetyCallouts.body: Several nights at 4.5 to 5 hours in a hot room, plus a sharp jump in easy heart rate, is a load your body is telling you about. Prioritise sleep this week, hydrate aggressively, and if the elevated heart rate and drained feeling persist once the AC is back and you are sleeping normally, please check in with a doctor rather than training through it.
